title: CATL becomes China’s largest heavy-duty battery swapping operator
gist: CATL bought China Power's 24.87% stake in Qiyuan Green Power for RMB2.6bn ($380m), lifting its holding to ~30% and, combined with its own QIJI Energy network, making CATL China's largest heavy-duty truck battery-swapping operator.

insights.claim: CATL bought the entire 24.87% stake in Qiyuan Green Power previously held by China Power (a subsidiary of State Power Investment Corporation) for RMB2.6 billion (about USD380 million), becoming Qiyuan's largest shareholder and raising CATL's total stake in the company to roughly 30%.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A discrete, priced M&A transaction (RMB2.6bn / ~30% stake) gives investors a hard valuation data point for China's heavy-duty EV battery-swapping infrastructure segment.
insights.quote: CATL bought the entirety of the 24.87% stake held by China Power, a subsidiary of the State Power Investment Corporation for RMB2.6 billion (USD380 million).

insights.claim: Qiyuan Green Power is China's largest heavy-duty truck battery-swapping network operator, running over 1,800 stations nationwide and holding more than 70% market share across heavy-truck use cases including mining zones.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A single operator holding >70% share of heavy-truck battery swapping signals high infrastructure concentration and barriers to entry in China's heavy-duty EV logistics segment.
insights.quote: Qiyuan currently leads the market with over 1,800 stations nationwide, giving it a market share of over 70% across various heavy-truck settings, including mining zones.
insights.locator: The move helps CATL to secure Qiyuan’s battery swapping infrastructure

insights.claim: By combining its enlarged Qiyuan stake with its own QIJI Energy battery-swapping network, CATL has become China's largest heavy-duty battery-swapping operator overall.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: CATL is vertically integrating swapping infrastructure on top of its cell/pack manufacturing dominance, a move toward standardized, CATL-controlled swappable-battery ecosystems for heavy trucks that could lock in downstream demand and pricing power.
insights.quote: Combined with CATL’s own QIJI Energy battery swapping network, this move makes the company China’s largest heavy-duty battery swapping operator.
insights.locator: Combined with CATL’s own QIJI Energy
